meta.description: Every 15 minutes, knock on POST /webhook/ask-human and alert if the door is not there. Built after that endpoint returned 404 for an unknown period: an orphaned webhook registration (from a workflow-ID rename) squatted the path, so the workflow was ACTIVE and the door was shut. Nothing noticed, because the only symptom was agents silently having no way to reach a human. WHAT IT PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: n8n answers a registered webhook with 200 'Workflow was started' before the workflow runs, so 200 proves the PATH IS REGISTERED and nothing about the run. That is precisely the failure being watched (404 = deregistered), and it is not a check that the ask flow works end to end. It also cannot detect n8n being down — a probe hosted inside n8n cannot report its own absence; container health covers that. Alerts on the SECOND consecutive failure, not the first: one blip is usually a restart, and paging on it trains everyone to ignore the alert. Re-raises every 4th failure (hourly) so a forgotten outage does not fade, and sends one info message on recovery. Counter state lives in workflow static data, which survives restarts but NOT a re-import of this workflow.
